aspects.says: allMatch on an empty stream returns true, the same identity as and, so an empty input passes an all-elements check.
basis: section:Optional Criteria Reduce from the Operator's Identity: x -> true for and, x -> false for or
aspects.reason: a one-line consequence of the identity the issue-search practice already grades; a test of it would only repeat that edge

aspects.says: Pattern.asPredicate tests find(), so it accepts input with the pattern anywhere in it; asMatchPredicate tests matches(), the whole input, and ^...$ with asPredicate still accepts a trailing line terminator.
basis: section:asPredicate Finds the Pattern Anywhere; asMatchPredicate Needs the Whole String

aspects.says: BiPredicate and IntPredicate have and, or and negate but no static not or isEqual.
basis: section:BiPredicate and IntPredicate Compose Like Predicate, Without not or isEqual
aspects.reason: which static helpers each interface has is enforced by the compiler, so no wrong solution compiles for a test to catch

aspects.says: An optional criterion whose field is empty is left out rather than reduced, because the or-reduction of nothing is x -> false and empties the result.
basis: section:Optional Criteria Reduce from the Operator's Identity: x -> true for and, x -> false for or

aspects.says: Removing inside a for-each throws ConcurrentModificationException at the next next(), except when the removal makes hasNext() false, and then the last element is silently never tested.
basis: section:removeIf Is the Safe Way to Remove While Iterating, and an Immutable List Refuses It Even When Nothing Matches

aspects.says: An unmodifiable list such as List.of or List.copyOf throws UnsupportedOperationException from removeIf even when no element matches; Arrays.asList throws only when one does.
basis: section:removeIf Is the Safe Way to Remove While Iterating, and an Immutable List Refuses It Even When Nothing Matches

aspects.says: Predicate.isEqual tests Objects.equals, so a null target or a null element is a value; c.equals(w) throws at a null element and w::equals throws when created with a null w.
basis: section:Predicate.isEqual Is Null-Safe on Both Sides; equals Called Through a Lambda Is Not

aspects.says: Reducing a list of predicates starts from x -> true for and and from x -> false for or; the other identity, or orElse(x -> false) on an empty list, rejects or accepts everything.
basis: section:Optional Criteria Reduce from the Operator's Identity: x -> true for and, x -> false for or

aspects.says: Collection.removeIf removes every matching element from the collection itself without skipping any, where removing inside an index loop or a for-each skips elements or throws ConcurrentModificationException.
basis: section:removeIf Is the Safe Way to Remove While Iterating, and an Immutable List Refuses It Even When Nothing Matches

aspects.says: In a parallel stream a stateful predicate's answer depends on the order threads test elements, so even a thread-safe seen-set keeps an arbitrary element per key; a collector keeps the first.
basis: section:A Predicate That Remembers Answers Differently in Parallel and on Its Second Use

aspects.says: A predicate that keeps a seen-set remembers across uses, so built once and reused it rejects on its second use what it accepted on its first.
basis: section:A Predicate That Remembers Answers Differently in Parallel and on Its Second Use

aspects.says: takeWhile returns the leading run of elements that pass and stops at the first false, and dropWhile returns the rest, so on input that is not ordered they differ from filter.
basis: section:filter Keeps Every Match; takeWhile Stops at the First false
